lanes.summary: I have reviewed the diff against the requirements of PMAT-3750. The PR successfully replaces all whole-file reads of models in the `apr qa` capability predicates with bounded header reads, significantly reducing peak RSS and preventing OOM risks on large models. It introduces a robust bounded reading mechanism in `model_header.rs` (starting at 16 MiB and doubling up to 256 MiB) for GGUF, and correctly uses `data_offset` for APR files. The implementation correctly reuses `MappedGGUFModel` where appropriate to avoid duplicate mapping. Furthermore, it provides the required ledger of all production and test `std::fs::read` occurrences, demonstrating that each was audited. The test suite correctly forks a subprocess to measure peak RSS without test framework pollution, enforcing the memory bounds. The changes directly satisfy `done_when 1`, `done_when 2`, and `done_when 3` of the ticket. I found no weakened gates or unrequested changes.

The diff perfectly addresses PMAT-3750 by replacing excessive `std::fs::read` and `to_vec` copies with bounded header reads and mmap-backed access (`MappedGGUFModel`). Peak RSS checks are correctly enforced through a subprocess test (`peak_rss_probe`), and the sibling sweep ledger correctly identifies and assigns verdicts to all `std::fs::read` occurrences in the production codebase. No capability gates are weakened, and the file-reading bounds are strictly enforced.

The diff flawlessly fulfills all acceptance criteria for PMAT-3750 PR A. It introduces bounded header readers (using `take().read_to_end()` to cap sizes) to replace full-file reads across the `apr qa` predicates. It provides a comprehensive audit of all `std::fs::read` occurrences in the specified crates, recording their status and justifications. The requested test against a sparse multi-GB fixture correctly spawns a probe to measure peak RSS against a precise bound. Furthermore, the provided GX10 measurements document a drop from 36.2GB to 19.3GB peak RSS (and to 45MiB on the capability gates alone), matching the objective perfectly. No refutations were found.
